archetype: Mardu LIFEGAIN-DRAIN COMBO on an aristocrats chassis, driven from the command zone — v2.1.0 (decklist sha a872115f…, merged from branch mean-v2 and sleeved on printed proxies 2026-10-20; fourteen swaps on the scan-confirmed v2.0.1). The list holds TWO loss-to-gain halves (Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Exquisite Blood) and FOUR gain-to-loss halves (Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose; Sanguine Bond; Enduring Tenacity; Marauding Blight-Priest), which is the 2x4 = 8 fully-contained two-card infinites deck-facts and bracket_report.json count; five of the eight pairings are checker-passed as deterministic table-kills (stacks 001 Exquisite+Vito, 004 Conqueror+Vito, 005 Bond+Exquisite, 006 Bond+Conqueror, 012 Tenacity+Conqueror) and the three Blight-Priest / Exquisite+Tenacity pairings are candidates only. Four tutors (Demonic, Vampiric, Enlightened, Diabolic Intent) back the loop; Edgar Markov's eminence mints a 1/1 Vampire on each of the 33 Vampire creature spells in the 99 without ever being cast; five free sacrifice outlets and Bloodghast turn those bodies into death drains (Cruel Celebrant, Vraan, Blood Artist, Vein Ripper, Anje) and death draw (Morbid Opportunist, Liliana, Crossway Troublemakers, Erebos, Clavileño); and four Vampires deny the table before the loop shows (Anowon's edict, Drana and Linvala's lock, Captivating Vampire's anthem-and-steal, Charismatic Conqueror's tax). Bracket floor 4 (Optimized): five Game Changers plus eight two-card infinites that assemble at mana value <= 6; DeckCheck read the same list at 46/96, their Bracket 4 (2026-10-20). The pilot's profile for this version, in his words: fast, threatening, bracket 4; life gain + life drain as the core; tokens into bigger threats; targeted removal; interaction and draw critical; once the combo pieces are out the table targets the Vampires, so as much protection and interaction as possible. In strategy:conversion.kill-pattern's terms this is the minority aristocrat Edgar whose 'compact closer is the gain-to-loss loop', not the combat Edgar the primers describe.

role_assignment.default_role: CONTROL-WITH-INEVITABILITY by Duke's test, not the beatdown v1.1.1 was. strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock: 'if one player is virtually guaranteed to win a game that goes long enough, that player has it — and knowing whether it's you decides your role', and in a pod 'engines are the default winning plan'. v2.1.0 owns the long game on paper: eight contained two-card loops, five of them checker-passed table-kills from ANY nonzero gain (stacks 001, 004, 005, 006, 012 — each resolves with no mana and no cards spent, retargeting every iteration), and four tutors, which strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors prices as 'k tutors plus the card act like k+1 copies of every card' — five effective copies of each half, '31% of openers'. The goldfish (seed 42, 10,000 games, model b025d0102196, this sha) draws a full pair in 22.1% of games by turn 10 and 10.8% by turn 6 unassisted, 57.3% and 33.3% tutor-assisted (goldfish.py: the _assisted figures credit tutors, the plain ones exclude them). So the role is seat-relative per strategy:whos-the-beatdown ('assign per-threat, not per-game'): against the fair decks you are the control — drain, deny, draw, and let the table spend its answers on each other (strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry: 'hold removal until the threat is pointed at you'); against a FASTER combo seat (log 004: a tutored two-card infinite closed first) you are the beatdown and must race or disrupt (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy: 'against combo … the last profitable moment is now'). The clock that backs the role is modest: median goldfish kill turn 8 (mean 8.37; 44.7% by 8, 81.3% by 10, 18.7% never by 10) with no blockers and no interaction — a CLOCK, not a win rate — and cumulative modelled drain only 6.3 by turn 10 because the death channel is an average rate (0.858 own deaths per turn, read off a 200-game Forge run on the V3 list) that cannot represent a sacrifice burst. The loop is the inevitability; combat is the fallback.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: strategy:pivot-point: 'The pivot is usually triggered by a concrete event — a resolved engine, a wrath, a key removal spell spent … Plan for it before it happens: hold the protection spell for the turn you commit, not after.' This list's concrete events: (1) ONE HALF ON THE BATTLEFIELD AND THE OTHER CASTABLE — any of Conqueror / Exquisite Blood with any of Vito / Bond / Tenacity (Blight-Priest pairings unverified). From that board the next life-gain event starts the loop (stacks 001/004/006/012 seed from 'any source'), and because Conqueror and Exquisite Blood trigger on ANY opponent's loss, the seed may be the table's own combat — a candidate line below, not yet a stack. strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window sets the commit test: 'assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing', and 'sequence the scariest piece last'. Here the scariest piece is the CREATURE half: Conqueror is 'strictly more fragile than the enchantment version' (stack 004 — a priority window for instant-speed creature removal every iteration), Tenacity is the resilient half (stack 012: destroy or -X/-X returns it as an enchantment with the drain ability intact; only exile, bounce, a countered return trigger, enchantment removal after one return, or removal on Conqueror break it). So land the enchantment half first and the body last, the turn you can protect it. (2) A TUTOR IN HAND WITH A HALF ON BOARD — Vampiric Tutor at an opponent's end step (strategy:tempo.sequencing: 'prefer committing at the end step before your own turn so the table's chances to respond are spent'), Demonic Tutor on your turn with mana for the half, Enlightened Tutor to the top for Exquisite Blood, Sanguine Bond or Tenacity (all enchantment cards), Diabolic Intent as a tutor that is also a death. (3) EDGAR ON THE BATTLEFIELD — Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat are free and Akroma's Will chooses both modes only 'if you control a commander', which eminence in the command zone does not satisfy; casting Edgar (goldfish: by turn 6 in 69.8% of games, mean 5.78) is the cheapest way to hold two free answers on the commit turn (strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance: 'the engine's hub justifies constant protection down plus a held response on the pivot turn'; strategy:multiplayer.zonal-commander: 'cast it when the body closes or protects'). (4) A WRATH ON THE STACK with a free outlet and a death payoff out — the pivot that is also the defence (strategy:aristocrats.wipe-insurance: 'a wrath on the stack is answered by sacrificing the whole board in response — each body a card, the drains firing on the way out'). From ahead, hedge: 'deploy only what you need, simplify, bank protection' (strategy:resource-hedging); from behind, find the line that wins if they do not have it and commit.

engines.engine: The drain loop set — the deck's kill. Loss-to-gain halves: Bloodthirsty Conqueror ('Whenever an opponent loses life, you gain that much life') and Exquisite Blood (same text on an enchantment). Gain-to-loss halves: Vito ('Whenever you gain life, target opponent loses that much life'), Sanguine Bond (identical), Enduring Tenacity (identical, plus a death-return clause), Marauding Blight-Priest ('each opponent loses 1 life' per gain event). deck-facts: 8 contained lines, 8 two-card infinites, none assuming the commander. CHECKER-PASSED, so fact: 001 Exquisite+Vito (38 iterations kill three seats at 2 per loop), 004 Conqueror+Vito (13 iterations, two seats), 005 Bond+Exquisite, 006 Bond+Conqueror, 012 Tenacity+Conqueror (21 iterations, two seats; the return clause keeps the loop running through destroy). NOT verified: Exquisite+Tenacity, Blight-Priest with either half. strategy:life-as-resource.lifegain-engine.bond-blood: 'holding both halves is a declaration the pregame conversation has to carry' and 'price the pair by what it costs the bracket, not by how often it assembles' — the pilot has priced it: bracket 4, 'infinite combos are welcome here' (CONTEXT.md). Scaling matters off-loop too: Vito, Bond and Tenacity are AMOUNT-scaled, Blight-Priest and Celebrant COUNT-scaled (strategy:conversion.yield), so a 6-power Vish Kal hit through Vito is six aimed drain, while a stream of 1-life refunds through Vito is one a fire. Goldfish: a pair drawn 22.1% of games by turn 10 (10.8% by 6); tutor-assisted 57.3% (33.3%).
engines.evidence: deck-facts combos (8 contained, 8 two-card infinites) + bracket_report.two_card_infinites + verified stacks 001, 004, 005, 006, 012 (checker.verdict pass) + goldfish target 'THE SURVIVING INFINITE' 0.221 / 0.573 assisted + oracle text

engines.engine: The loop's consistency: Demonic Tutor, Vampiric Tutor (instant — end-step, to the top), Enlightened Tutor (artifact or enchantment to the top: reaches Exquisite Blood, Sanguine Bond, Enduring Tenacity, Anointed Procession, Urza's Incubator, Ashnod's Altar) and Diabolic Intent (sacrifice a creature as a cost — a tutor that is also a death trigger for every converter on board). strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors: 'a named card is 7.1% of your opening seven' and 'k tutors plus the card act like k+1 copies of every card' — with four tutors each half reads like five copies, '31% of openers', and the two-by-four pairing means no single card is the loop's point of failure (deck-audit names only Anguished Unmaking and Bloodletter as one-card components). The cost the doc states and the pilot accepts: 'the more tutors you play, the less actual cards you get to play' and tutor count is 'a power-level lever' — bracket_report counts three of them among the five Game Changers. strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density's cEDH rule fits the layering here: 'overlap pieces, so five cards support four combos' — six pieces support eight.
engines.evidence: oracle text + bracket_report.tutors / game_changers + deck-audit tutors axis (4) + goldfish assisted-vs-unassisted spread (0.221 -> 0.573)

engines.engine: Eminence: 'Whenever you cast another Vampire spell, if Edgar is in the command zone or on the battlefield, create a 1/1 black Vampire creature token.' Enumerated from cards.json: 33 of the 37 creature cards in the 99 are Vampires (the four that are not: Enduring Tenacity, Erebos, Ingris Stingerquill, Morbid Opportunist), so 33 casts are tokens; Bloodghast's landfall return is not a cast and makes none. strategy:multiplayer.zonal-commander: eminence 'affects the Battlefield from the Command Zone, so they can shape games even if they are never played' — and its GAP line is this deck's exact question: 'nobody gives the threshold at which the body is worth the cast'. v2.1.0 makes the threshold concrete: with Edgar on the battlefield Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat cost nothing and Akroma's Will takes both modes, so the cast buys the protection the pilot's profile asks for, and Urza's Incubator (chosen type Vampire) makes the 6-drop a 4-drop. Goldfish: cast by turn 6 in 69.8% of games, mean turn 5.78, median 6; the attack trigger (counters on each Vampire) is a bonus to the big-Vampire line, not an engine. Stacks 002 and 010 (checker-passed on earlier lists) resolved eminence through the doublers with Edgar never cast and established the replacement-effect arithmetic (two doublers, 1 -> 4); Elspeth and Anointed Procession are the two doublers left in v2.1.0.
engines.evidence: oracle text + cards.json creature-type enumeration (33 Vampires of 37) + goldfish_metrics.commander (0.698 by t6) + checker-passed stacks 002, 010 + goldfish target 'A token multiplier' 0.371

engines.engine: Death drains, read per strategy:aristocrats.drain-scope ('read the trigger and the drain separately … each-opponent for the race, targeted for the kill'). EACH-OPPONENT: Cruel Celebrant (your creature or planeswalker dies: 1 each, you gain 1), Vraan, Executioner Thane (your creatures die: 2 each, once per turn), Anje ({2}, sacrifice a creature or Blood token: 2 each). TARGETED: Blood Artist (ANY creature dies: target player loses 1), Vein Ripper (ANY creature dies: target opponent loses 2, you gain 2; ward — sacrifice a creature). Also-gains: Edgar, Ancient Bloodlord (1 life per death), Tithe Drinker's extort, Sanctum Seeker and Wispdrinker on attack and entry. Every one of these gains is a LOOP SEED once a gain-to-loss half is out, and every loss they inflict is a seed once Conqueror or Exquisite Blood is out — which is why the drains are the deck's fair plan and its ignition at the same time. Yield arithmetic from strategy:conversion.yield: with Celebrant, Vraan, Artist and Ripper all out, one death moves 3+2+2 = 7 life off a three-opponent table plus Vraan's 6 once a turn. Goldfish: a death drain drawn in 60.4% of games (44.1% by turn 6). CAVEAT the doc states for this exact bench: a creature converter 'dies to the same sweeper that kills the fodder' and 'this bench's Edgar kept its most-included one on the battlefield 0.6 turns a game' (strategy:conversion.durability) — Exquisite Blood and Sanguine Bond are the converters that outlive the fodder.
engines.evidence: oracle text + goldfish target 'A drain that fires when a creature DIES' 0.604 / by t6 0.441 + goldfish_metrics.drain (cumulative 6.32 by t10, 69.4% of games draining) + goldfish meta death_rate source (Forge standard-v3, V3 list)

engines.engine: Outlets and fodder — strategy:aristocrats: 'an aristocrats turn needs three things — fodder, an outlet, a payoff' and 'price outlets by activation first'. FREE (no mana): Viscera Seer, Ashnod's Altar (makes {C}{C}), Phyrexian Tower (a land: {T}, sacrifice a creature: {B}{B}), Vish Kal (counters equal to the victim's power), Yahenni (indestructible) — the five in goldfish_targets' free-outlet group, drawn in 69.1% of games (53.3% by turn 6). MANA-GATED: Master of Dark Rites ({T}, sacrifice: {B}{B}{B} for Vampire/Cleric/Demon SPELLS only — deck-facts' restricted-mana note: it cannot pay an activated ability), Edgar, Ancient Bloodlord ({2}), Erebos ({1}{B}), Anje ({2}). ONE-SHOT: Diabolic Intent, Bloodtithe Harvester (itself), Reactor Raid. deck-facts role count: sac-outlet 8. Fodder comes all three of Gottfried's ways: eminence tokens, cheap bodies (23 nonland entries at mana value <= 2), and recursion — Bloodghast ('can't block', returns on every land drop) is the v2.1.0 fuel that never runs out, and Charismatic Conqueror, Preacher, Elenda, Bloodline Keeper, Liliana, Elspeth, Ingris and Clavileño all mint bodies. The free outlet is also the wipe answer (strategy:aristocrats.wipe-insurance) and the doc's warning applies: a free outlet is 'a fragile, highly suspicious permanent' that 'eats the removal your payoffs would draw'. Goldfish sacrifices: 1.405 by turn 10 — a floor, since the death channel is an averaged rate, and CONTEXT.md's standing Forge finding is that the AI 'fetches Vish Kal and sits on Exquisite Blood', so no Forge figure prices this stage.
engines.evidence: goldfish_targets free-outlet group (5 cards) + goldfish target 0.691 / 0.533 + deck-facts roles (sac-outlet 8, sac-cost 6) and restricted_mana note + goldfish_metrics.mean_sacrifices_by_turn (1.405 @10) + oracle text

engines.engine: Death-triggered draw — the pilot's required axis ('runs out of steam' is the cause on logs 001, 002, 003, 006) and the v2.1.0 objective. Enumerated: Morbid Opportunist ('one or more other creatures die … once each turn'), Liliana, Dreadhorde General (every creature of yours), Crossway Troublemakers (a Vampire of yours dies: pay 2 life, draw), Erebos (another creature of yours dies: pay 2 life, draw), Clavileño (an attacking Vampire becomes a Demon with 'when this dies, draw a card and create a tapped 4/3 flier'), Reactor Raid (sacrifice: draw two, once). Steady draw beside it: Phyrexian Arena, Welcoming Vampire and Caretaker's Talent (entries, once a turn), Preacher, Twilight Prophet, Castle Locthwain, Blood tokens from Anje and Bloodtithe Harvester. The split is the one strategy:card-advantage.plan-draw prescribes for exactly this failure — 'a typal or aristocrat midrange that empties its hand by turn 7 wants the slots split, not stacked — steady draw live in the enabler-less keep, the rest on-plan so a sacrifice or a swing draws the next wave; no primer gives the split' — and its pricing rule ('price life-costed draw against the drain that refunds it') is why Crossway's and Erebos's 2 life a card is cheap beside Conqueror or Exquisite Blood. strategy:aristocrats.wipe-insurance names the shape: 'death draw pays nothing until bodies die, then in a burst, exactly when the hand is empty' — and 'hold the second outlet and one draw body back for the rebuild'. Measured: mean extra cards by turn 8 1.81 and by turn 10 3.12 (goldfish, seed 42); the mean-v2 guard 'extra cards by T8 >= 1.65' read 1.7639, met (net_change objective_grade). The model prices 8 of 16 draw cards and names the rest (meta.card_advantage.draw_not_modelled: Anje, Bloodtithe Harvester, Clavileño, Crossway, Erebos, Midgar, Preacher, Savai Triome), and deck-audit reads card-advantage UNDER (7 vs 10) with nine possibly-uncounted cards named — so both figures are floors. strategy:card-advantage: 'engines that out-draw three players are the format's defining advantage'.
engines.evidence: oracle text + goldfish target 'A draw engine drawn' 0.752 / 0.636 + goldfish_metrics.mean_extra_cards_drawn_by_turn (1.81 @8, 3.124 @10) + branches/mean-v2/net_change.json objective_grade (1.7639 >= 1.65, met) + meta.card_advantage (8 of 16 modelled) + deck-audit card-advantage axis + log_causes.json

engines.engine: Proactive denial on Vampire bodies, the v2.1.0 package the pilot asked for and the only one the goldfish cannot see (goldfish_targets _v210_note: Anowon, Drana and Linvala and Exotic Orchard 'sit in no group: the goldfish has no opponents to tax, lock or edict'). Anowon: each upkeep every player sacrifices a non-Vampire creature — three opponents' boards shrink and yours does not, EXCEPT that you own four non-Vampire creatures (Enduring Tenacity, Erebos when devotion >= 5, Ingris Stingerquill, Morbid Opportunist) and Anowon bills you one of them each upkeep you control one; Tenacity sacrificed this way returns as an enchantment (candidate line). Drana and Linvala: 'activated abilities of creatures your opponents control can't be activated' and you gain them all — a lock on every creature-based outlet, mana dork and commander ability at the table (not on artifact or enchantment abilities). Captivating Vampire: +1/+1 to other Vampires and 'tap five untapped Vampires: gain control of target creature. It becomes a Vampire' — which reads as exempting the stolen creature from Anowon and from Olivia's Wrath (a candidate line below, not a stack). Charismatic Conqueror: every untapped entry on their side is a tap or a lifelink token for you — strategy:conversion.passive-tax's two prices apply to it: 'the trigger reads an opponent's state, which they can change' (they may tap), and 'taxing the whole table makes you everyone's problem at once'. strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial, read from the applying side: 'one piece is an inconvenience; the compounding second and third are the lock', and your opponents' answer is forced to be velocity or removal under the edict. strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry licenses the whole class: 'effects that tax or drain every opponent at once'. Each is a Vampire cast — an eminence token — so denial costs no tempo on the fodder line. DeckCheck's rescan is the one instrument that read it: I2 (proactive denial) F -> B on the same deck id, 28/96 -> 46/96. Forge cast checks (branches/mean-v2/cast_proofs.json, 8-game shells): Anowon cast 6 / triggered 15, Drana and Linvala cast 4, Captivating cast 3 — all PLAYED.
engines.evidence: oracle text + cards.json enumeration of own non-Vampire creatures (4) + goldfish_targets _v210_note + deckcheck.json readings (I2 F -> B, 28 -> 46 of 96) + branches/mean-v2/cast_proofs.json verdicts

engines.engine: Velocity: Urza's Incubator (Vampire creature spells cost {2} less — 33 spells in the 99 plus Edgar from the command zone) with ten ramp copies (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Orzhov and Rakdos Signets, Talismans of Conviction, Hierarchy and Indulgence, Ashnod's Altar, Master of Dark Rites, the Incubator itself) and Ancient Tomb. strategy:critical-mass: a linear deck's 'defense is speed, redundancy, and resilience, not answers' and 'know your number'. The number here is two permanents, so speed is how many Vampire casts and how much open mana reach the turn the second half lands. Measured (mana_analysis, this sha): on-curve with rocks W 0.927, B 0.916, R 0.907; sources with rocks W 24 / B 37 / R 22 against Karsten targets 22 / 36 / 22 — every colour at or over target for the first time (v1.1.1 was four black sources short); 12 of 35 lands enter tapped (34%, 'over the one-in-three budget'). Goldfish: 6.05 mana at turn 6, land drop hit 88.9% at turn 3 and 76.0% at turn 4, keep 77.9% of first sevens, 92.9% of kept hands act by turn 3. The cost the pilot named is cards-in-hand, not mana; the goldfish cannot price the Incubator's discount on the commander, so Edgar's cast turn is a floor. Forge cast check: Incubator cast 6 / held castable-uncast on 6 own turns — the AI sits on it, so any Forge rate is a floor on this engine too.
engines.evidence: oracle text + deck-audit ramp axis (10, at) + mana_analysis.json (on_curve_probability, sources, source_targets, enters_tapped) + goldfish_metrics (mana, land drops, opening_hand) + cast_proofs.json (Incubator held 6 turns)

engines.engine: Protection, enumerated against what it covers. BOARD-WIDE: Teferi's Protection (everything phases out, life can't change — the only card that covers Exquisite Blood, Sanguine Bond, Anointed Procession, Urza's Incubator, Phyrexian Arena, Elspeth and Liliana against a wipe), Akroma's Will (creatures: lifelink, indestructible, protection from each colour; both modes only with a commander on the battlefield), Flawless Maneuver (creatures indestructible; free with Edgar out). TARGETED: Deflecting Swat (retarget a spell or ability; free with Edgar out) — reaches any permanent and also turns an opposing edict-trigger or tutor. 'Free with Edgar out' is the stricter reading of 'if you control a commander' — eminence in the command zone is assumed NOT to satisfy it until a stack rules (candidate line below). SELF: Enduring Tenacity's return clause (stack 012), Vein Ripper's ward (sacrifice a creature — itself a death trigger), Yahenni (sacrifice another creature: indestructible), Erebos (indestructible). Boros Charm left in v2.1.0, so noncreature cover shrank to Teferi's Protection and Swat. Goldfish: a protection spell held in 60.6% of games (45.1% by turn 6) — the four instants only. strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite's budget line: 'answers to answers are a separate budget — 2-4 protection generic, 4-6 combo'; deck-audit counts 7 protection copies, AT the 5-7 band. strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance's taxonomy is the sequencing rule: single-use instants 'protect at the decisive moment and can cover the board', so hold them for the commit turn, and 'assume every held answer appears the moment you commit'. Interaction castable by turn 6 reads 18.1% in the goldfish though a piece is in hand 86.4% of the time — the structural half of 'cannot afford to hold up interaction'.
engines.evidence: oracle text (commander clauses read verbatim) + goldfish target 'Protection held for the swarm' 0.606 / 0.451 + goldfish_metrics.interaction_castable_by_turn (0.181 @6) and interaction_in_hand_by_turn (0.864 @6) + deck-audit protection axis (7, at) + stack 012 final_state

engines.engine: The big-Vampire line — the pilot's 'tokens into bigger threats'. Vish Kal (keep list, protected.json: 'never cut'): a 5/5 flying lifelinker that eats any creature for counters equal to its power and cashes them as -1/-1 per counter on a target creature — which kills an indestructible blocker (toughness 0 is not a destroy), the exact spot log 006 lost to. Elenda (counter per death, X lifelink tokens on death), Cordial Vampire (a counter on every Vampire per death), Captivating Vampire and Bloodline Keeper's back face (lords), Clavileño (an attacker becomes a Demon that dies into a card and a 4/3 flier), Edgar's attack trigger. Through Vito, Bond or Tenacity a lifelink hit is an AMOUNT-scaled drain (strategy:life-as-resource.lifegain-engine: 'a six-power lifelink body connecting is six aimed drain'), and Crossway Troublemakers gives every attacking Vampire lifelink. strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry: 'board quality beats board quantity … a single scaling permanent out-values a fair board against three players'. The limit is strategy:conversion.combat-channel's three taxes — blockers divide width, an attack picks one enemy and opens you to two, once a turn — which this bench measured when a lordless refactor dropped combat damage 29.07 -> 18.20. The two lords are the exposure strategy:deckbuilding.typal-density.lord-exposure prices: 'every lord past the creature floor is +1 on every body and one more body under the wrath'; the pilot's own rule is that a flat anthem is too slow and Captivating earns its slot on the steal, not the +1. Goldfish: a lord drawn 50.6% (35.7% by 6); board power 8.6 at turn 6, 18.6 at turn 10.
engines.evidence: oracle text + protected.json (Vish Kal) + goldfish target 'A Vampire lord or anthem' 0.506 / 0.357 + goldfish_metrics.combat.mean_board_power_by_turn + captains log 006 (log.jsonl) + CONTEXT.md 'What the pilot does not want'

engines.engine: The drain doubler: 'If an opponent would lose life during your turn, they lose twice that much life instead.' Every finite drain on your turn — Celebrant, Vraan, Artist, Ripper, Sanctum Seeker, Wispdrinker, Tithe Drinker's extort, Twilight Prophet, Anje — doubles, and so does every loop iteration (moot once the loop is deterministic, decisive when the loop is broken mid-way and the pilot is counting a finite drain to lethal). Stacks 003 and 007 (checker-passed on earlier lists) priced it with Sanctum Seeker and the end step. strategy:conversion.yield: 'Noncombat-damage doublers scale this channel the way anthems scale combat'. It is a one-card component (deck-audit single_points_of_failure: 7.1% of opening sevens) and the goldfish pairs it with Sanctum Seeker in only 4.5% of games (1.9% by turn 6; 33.0% tutor-assisted) — a windfall, not a plan, and the right Demonic Tutor target only when the loop is already answered.
engines.evidence: oracle text + goldfish target 'THE DRAIN DOUBLER' 0.045 / 0.019 / 0.330 assisted + deck-audit single_points_of_failure + checker-passed stacks 003, 007

candidate_missing_lines.title: The three unverified pairings: Exquisite Blood + Enduring Tenacity (two enchantment-type halves — the most removal-resistant loop in the 99), and Marauding Blight-Priest with Conqueror or with Exquisite Blood, where 'each opponent loses 1' per gain event makes three loss events per iteration — does the chain widen rather than loop, and is it deterministic enough to shortcut?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: combo_details lists all three as 'Infinite lifeloss' two-card lines (popularity 74,875 / 60,315 / 48,102) and deck-facts counts them among the eight contained infinites, but only five pairings carry a checker-passed stack (001, 004, 005, 006, 012). Blight-Priest is COUNT-scaled (strategy:conversion.yield) while every verified half is AMOUNT-scaled, so the walk differs: one gain -> three opponents each lose 1 -> Conqueror triggers three times -> three Blight-Priest triggers. The shortcut legality under 732 with a branching trigger count is exactly what a checker should rule on.

candidate_missing_lines.title: The loop that starts on someone else's turn: Conqueror (or Exquisite Blood) and Vito (or Bond, or Tenacity) on the battlefield, and an opponent attacks ANOTHER opponent — does that combat damage seed the infinite, who chooses Vito's targets, and can the pilot decline to start it?
cards: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Conqueror and Exquisite Blood read 'Whenever an opponent loses life' with no 'you' qualifier, and the five verified stacks seed from 'any source' of gain; the one step before — an opponent's loss to a third party's attack, Purphoros ping (log 005's predator) or their own Phyrexian Arena — is not walked in any stack. Both triggers are mandatory, so the answer decides whether 'the table targets the vamps once the pieces are out' (the pilot's profile) is a threat they can even wait on, and whether a Forge or paper table can be killed on an opponent's turn under Bloodletter's 'during your turn' clause not applying.

candidate_missing_lines.title: The wipe answered in response: Viscera Seer, Cruel Celebrant, Vraan, Blood Artist, Morbid Opportunist and Liliana out, a sweeper on the stack, sacrifice eight Vampires (two of them Clavileño's Demons) — cards drawn, life moved per seat, which once-per-turn clauses cap it, and what survives for the rebuild.

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: The matchup v2.1.0 was rebuilt for. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math: 'assume the wrath — over a four-player game one is near-certain — so deploy in waves, hold a rebuild package'; three of five logged losses were wipes (log_causes 001, 002, 006, all on v1.x lists). Three answers now exist. (1) strategy:aristocrats.wipe-insurance: with any of the five free outlets and a death payoff out, sacrifice in response — Celebrant/Vraan drain the table, Morbid/Liliana/Crossway/Erebos refill the hand, Clavileño's Demons leave 4/3 fliers behind (candidate line above). (2) strategy:conversion.durability: 'put the converter on a type the wipe does not read' — Exquisite Blood and Sanguine Bond are enchantments, Enduring Tenacity returns as one, so a creature wipe leaves the loop's safer halves standing while the fodder dies INTO them. (3) Eminence rebuilds from a zone no wipe touches, and Bloodghast comes back on the next land. Cover is enumerated honestly: only Teferi's Protection phases out the enchantments, Elspeth and Liliana; Akroma's Will and Flawless Maneuver read 'creatures you control'. Rule for the second sweeper: 'redeploy worst-first, keeping the best threat in hand' — the best threat here is the second loop half, not a body. Against the counterspell seat (log 001 lost two key spells), strategy:tempo.sequencing: strike 'in the window when opponents are tapped out', Vampiric Tutor at their end step, and read inaction as information (strategy:information.range-tells: 'they let the engine resolve: the counterspell isn't there').
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Two-sided now. As the VICTIM: strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial — 'taxes attack the velocity math directly, so recount your hand under the tax', and 'you rarely own the long game under an assembling lock, so you are the beatdown, racing the lock's completion'. 23 nonland entries at mana value <= 2 are the velocity a tax halves; Urza's Incubator's {2} discount is the counter-tax on 33 spells; the five free outlets and eminence are the parts of the engine a Sphere cannot touch. Outs, enumerated from deck-audit's interaction axis: Anguished Unmaking is the ONLY catch-all for a noncreature lock piece (one card, 7.1% of openers — the single point of failure the audit names), Deflecting Swat retargets a tax trigger, Path and the edicts answer creature-based stax, and breadth leaves graveyard and LAND uncovered (interaction-breadth: 3 of 5 classes), so a land-based lock must be raced or tutored out of (Demonic Tutor -> Anguished Unmaking). As the APPLIER: Anowon, Drana and Linvala, Charismatic Conqueror and Captivating Vampire are a creature-shaped stax package that each-opponent decks are 'hit hardest' by — 'one piece is an inconvenience; the compounding second and third are the lock' — and every piece is a Vampire cast. Name the out early: 'the removal or velocity that breaks the piece that beats you, not the scariest piece'.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: The matchup the gain half is for. strategy:life-as-resource: 'only the last point matters' and 'switching from spending to defending one turn before it matters, not one after' — the licence to pay Crossway, Erebos, Phyrexian Arena, Anguished Unmaking, Vampiric Tutor and the painlands early and to stop the turn a burn or drain seat has reach. strategy:life-as-resource.lifegain-engine: 'life gain is a buffer until something converts it' — Conqueror or Exquisite Blood alone refund EVERY point any opponent loses to anyone, so an aggro seat attacking the table is paying you; with a gain-to-loss half out those refunds are aimed drain. Bodies: 1/1 eminence tokens chump and then feed an outlet (a chump into Viscera Seer is a death trigger, not a lost card), Charismatic Conqueror makes their untapped haste creatures a choice between entering tapped and giving you a lifelink token, and Vish Kal / Crossway Troublemakers (attacking Vampires have deathtouch and lifelink) make blocks pay. strategy:combat-math.racing: 'you cannot race three life totals — races there are two-player subgames … spend the minimum that wins yours and keep watching the other seats'. Assign per seat (strategy:whos-the-beatdown): control against the aggro seat's clock, beatdown by drain against the two developing seats. Goldfish bodies: 4.3 at turn 6, 10.0 at turn 10 — enough chaff to never block with a payoff.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: Inevitability against inevitability, so Duke's test decides: whoever is slower is the beatdown. Stack interaction is Deflecting Swat alone (a retarget, not a counter) plus Drana and Linvala's lock on creature activated abilities and Anowon / Liliana's -4 as edicts against creature-based combos — nothing touches an artifact or enchantment loop except Anguished Unmaking (instant: exile target nonland permanent) and Teferi's Protection as a one-turn fog on your own life total ('your life total can't change' stops a drain loop aimed at you for a turn; whether it stops the table's deaths is their problem). strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy: 'held answers rot — against combo, or lethal already on board, the last profitable moment is now' — spend Anguished Unmaking on the half you can see. Log 004 lost to a tutored two-card infinite; the pilot's pod-norm question from that night is answered by the list itself now (eight loops, four tutors, bracket 4 declared), and strategy:life-as-resource.lifegain-engine.bond-blood names the duty: 'a declaration the pregame conversation has to carry'. Threat perception is the real lever (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection: 'combo decks look non-threatening while advancing in secret, which is exactly why experienced tables hit the quiet ramp player'): your tells are Conqueror, Vito, Sanguine Bond, Exquisite Blood and Tenacity, and the deflection budget spends as each lands — land the enchantment half under cover of a drain-looking board, hold the body half with Edgar out and Swat free.
matchup_frames.vs_trigger_racer: Purphoros and Impact Tremors decks (log 005: 'the natural predator for mid-range aggro'; the 2026-09-03 Forge playgroup pod on v1.1.0 gave this seat 4 of 38 decided games against purphoros-pingers' 19). v2.1.0 changes the arithmetic twice. First, their pings to the OTHER two seats are losses Conqueror and Exquisite Blood refund to you, and with a gain-to-loss half out they are drains — candidate line above, not a stack. Second, Olivia's Wrath ('each non-Vampire creature gets -X/-X where X is the number of Vampires you control') is a one-sided sweeper against the token board that fuels their triggers, and Anowon edicts one of their non-Vampires every upkeep. The enchantment itself (Purphoros is indestructible) answers only to Anguished Unmaking or Swat; Elspeth's -3 and Liliana's -4 do not reach it. strategy:life-as-resource's switch applies: the moment a pinger is in range, stop paying life (Crossway, Erebos, Arena, Vampiric Tutor, Anguished Unmaking all bill you) — the frame's rule is that every life payment is a loop seed for THEM if they run a Conqueror-shaped card, and a clock on you if they do not.

overall_assessment: This deck plays the lifegain-drain combo game and uses aristocrats as its fair plan and its ignition — and v2.1.0 is the first list where the artifacts and the pilot's direction agree about it. The 99 holds two loss-to-gain halves and four gain-to-loss halves, five of the eight pairings are checker-passed table-kills from any nonzero gain (stacks 001, 004, 005, 006, 012), four tutors make each half read like five copies (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors), and the pilot has declared the bracket the pair costs (strategy:life-as-resource.lifegain-engine.bond-blood: 'price the pair by what it costs the bracket, not by how often it assembles'). Around the loop sits the engine strategy:aristocrats prices in three parts: fodder the command zone mints on 33 of 37 creature casts and Bloodghast replays on every land, five free outlets, and payoffs that split cleanly into each-opponent drains for the race (Celebrant, Vraan, Anje) and targeted ones for the kill (Artist, Vein Ripper) — strategy:aristocrats.drain-scope's rule — every one of which both seeds the loop and refills the hand through the death-draw package the version added for the pilot's named failure, running dry at turns seven and eight (extra cards by turn 8: 1.81 modelled, with eight of sixteen draw cards unpriced). The school that justifies the shape is strategy:conversion: 'the point of your engine is not to make resources … it is to win the game', and its corrections are the frame's two cautions. strategy:conversion.durability: a creature converter 'dies to the same sweeper that kills the fodder' — this bench's own Edgar kept its most-included one on the battlefield 0.6 turns a game — so the loop's resilient halves are the enchantments (Exquisite Blood, Sanguine Bond, the self-returning Tenacity) and the sequencing rule is enchantment first, body last, with Edgar on the battlefield so Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat are free on the commit turn (strategy:multiplayer.zonal-commander's GAP — when is the body worth the cast — has a concrete answer in this list). And strategy:conversion.kill-pattern: the literature 'supports the mechanism claim, not the timing one', so every turn number here is the bench's: median goldfish kill turn 8 with no blockers, a pair drawn by turn 6 in one game in nine unassisted and one in three with tutors, no Forge record on this sha and a Forge AI that the last audit showed tutoring Vish Kal and sitting on Exquisite Blood. Role follows: by Duke's inevitability test this deck is the CONTROL at most tables (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock: 'engines are the default winning plan'), the beatdown only against a faster combo seat, and the whole game is the pivot window (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window): 'assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal' — which is why the four denial Vampires matter strategically and not just as bodies: Anowon, Drana and Linvala, Captivating and Charismatic Conqueror spend the table's resources before the tells land, the only thing in the list the goldfish cannot see at all and the one DeckCheck's rescan moved most (I2 F -> B). The honest weaknesses: interaction breadth stops at creature/artifact/enchantment with Anguished Unmaking the lone catch-all (7.1% of openers), noncreature cover is Teferi's Protection and Swat only now that Boros Charm is gone, a third of the lands enter tapped in a deck whose profile says fast, and the deck still bills its own life on its draw and tutors (Crossway, Erebos, Phyrexian Arena, Preacher, Vampiric Tutor, Anguished Unmaking) and on its mana (three Talismans; the lands cost 9 life on entry and 8 per tap cycle, mana_analysis) — fine currency (strategy:life-as-resource) until a loop or a pinger is in range, when it is a seed for them. Nothing above is a result of play: v2.1.0 has no games, and the six logged losses were older lists.
gaps: No section on the FREE-WITH-A-COMMANDER spell class (Flawless Maneuver, Deflecting Swat, Akroma's Will's both-modes clause) as a protection budget, nor on how it interacts with an eminence commander the pilot would rather not cast. strategy:multiplayer.zonal-commander names the cast-threshold GAP and strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance prices protection OF the commander; this deck's question is protection UNLOCKED BY the commander. Best query hit for 'protecting combo pieces once the table targets you' was Threat Deflection at 0.37.

No section on PROACTIVE DENIAL FROM THE APPLYING SIDE — edicts and activated-ability locks carried on creature bodies (Anowon, Drana and Linvala) in a deck that is not a stax deck. The query 'stax taxes edict lock proactive denial' top-scored strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial at 0.41 (written for the victim; the frame read it in reverse) and strategy:conversion.passive-tax at 0.28 (upkeep damage taxes on artifacts, which it says explicitly is 'narrow'); neither prices an each-upkeep edict or a creature-ability lock as a pod effect, and DeckCheck's I2 is the only instrument that read the package at all.

No section on LOOP SEEDING BY THE TABLE: a loss-to-gain half makes every opponent's loss to anyone your trigger, so the combo can fire on an opponent's turn without the pilot acting. bond-blood covers intent and bracket, not the seed sources or the politics of a loop that starts by itself; the candidate line above routes the rules half to resolve-stack, the strategy half has no home.

No section on COMBAT-VERSUS-TRIGGER timing for this archetype — strategy:conversion.kill-pattern and strategy:conversion.combat-channel both declare the GAP explicitly ('no fetchable primer states a kill turn', 'no writer prices the damage-per-mana of an attack step against that of a trigger'). The handbook must keep every turn number as the bench's measurement.

No section on COST REDUCTION as velocity (Urza's Incubator, Herald's Horn-class effects) against rocks: the frame grounded it in strategy:critical-mass, which prices thresholds, not the discount. strategy:critical-mass.storm-math was not fetched this session and may cover part of it.

No section on PLAYING INTO A SWEEPER WITH A SELF-RETURNING PIECE (Enduring Tenacity-class 'dies -> returns as an enchantment'): strategy:conversion.durability covers type-line resilience in general; the specific play pattern — sacrifice Tenacity to your own Anowon or outlet to make it wipe-proof on purpose — is a candidate line and has no doc line.

No section on LIFE PAYMENTS AS A SEED FOR AN OPPONENT'S Conqueror-shaped card or pinger clock; strategy:life-as-resource gives the switch rule, not the drain-mirror case the pod actually presents (log 005's Vito mono-black seat, log 006's drain seats).

MEASUREMENT gaps the orchestrator should route rather than the doc: (a) no Forge record on sha a872115f, and the standing finding (CONTEXT.md, sim audit 2026-10-06) is that the AI tutors Vish Kal and sits on Exquisite Blood, so every Forge rate is a floor on the loop; (b) the goldfish's death channel is an averaged rate (0.858 own deaths per turn from a V3-list Forge run) and cannot price a sacrifice burst, so sacrifices 1.41 by turn 10 and cumulative drain 6.3 are floors; (c) 'THE SURVIVING INFINITE' counts both halves DRAWN, not resolved with protection up — the pivot-window rate is unmeasured; (d) deck-audit has no combo-aristocrats archetype override, so creatures read informational and card-advantage reads under against base targets; (e) engine.json is stale and failing on this sha and was not cited; (f) the five verified loop stacks were written on earlier lists and carry no decklist sha — their boards still hold because every named card is in the 99, but 012's preamble says Tenacity 'is NOT in the 99', which is no longer true and should be regenerated, not patched.

DECISION the orchestrator may surface: the pilot's profile says 'targeted removal' and 'interaction critical', and deck-audit reads interaction AT (8 removal in a 16-copy suite) but breadth UNDER with graveyard and land uncovered and one catch-all; whether the next slot is a second catch-all (restoring the Despark / Boros Charm cover the version cut) or stays on the profile package is a pilot call, and the frame does not pick.
